ref: 61.1 (Trollope 'LXI'; ANF heading 'Chapter 61'; chapter division as in Trollope/Otto)
greek: Μαρτύρομαι δὲ καὶ ἄλλο ὑμῖν, ὦ φίλοι, ἔφην, ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν δώσω, ὅτι ἀρχὴν πρὸ πάντων τῶν κτισμάτων ὁ Θεὸς γεγέννηκε δύναμιν τινὰ ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ λογικὴν, ἥτις καὶ δόξα κυρίου ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου καλεῖται, ποτὲ δὲ υἱὸς, ποτὲ δὲ σοφία, ποτὲ δὲ ἄγγελος, ποτὲ δὲ Θεὸς, ποτὲ δὲ κύριος καὶ λόγος, ποτὲ δὲ ἀρχιστράτηγον ἑαυτὸν λέγει, ἐν ἀνθρώπου μορφῇ φανέντα τῷ Ναυῆ Ἰησοῦ.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo Dialogus, vol. 1, Cambridge (sold by G. Bell, London), 1846; Greek text on PDF pp.133-134 (printed 123-124), read on the page image and checked against the PDF text layer and djvu OCR. Accents as printed. The Otto-based lemma 'ἀρχὴν πρὸ πάντων τῶν κτισμάτων ὁ θεὸς γεγέννηκε δύναμίν [τινα] ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ λογικήν' is quoted in Otto (see J6-13 file, PDF p.75).
english: Justin: I shall give you another testimony, my friends, from the Scriptures, that God begot before all creatures a Beginning, [who was] a certain rational power [proceeding] from Himself, who is called by the Holy Spirit, now the Glory of the Lord, now the Son, again Wisdom, again an Angel, then God, and then Lord and Logos; and on another occasion He calls Himself Captain, when He appeared in human form to Joshua the son of Nave (Nun).
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; revised for New Advent by Kevin Knight)
page: Greek: Trollope pp.123-124. English: page unknown (ANF online text has no page numbers).
edition: Trollope 1846 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: God begot before all creatures a rational power from Himself, which Scripture calls by many names (Glory, Son, Wisdom, Angel, God, Lord, Logos, Captain).
use: supports Trinitarian reading (a pre-existent divine Logos called God); the 'begot before creatures' wording is the source of the objection in J6-04 and J6-12
limits: Justin does not say homoousios. 'Power' and 'beginning' are the words Arians and Unitarians cite. The list includes 'Angel' and 'Captain' (Josh 5:14), which opponents read as a created messenger. Trollope's note on the first clause (pp.123-124) reports that many commentators take 'ἀρχήν' as accusative in apposition to 'δύναμιν' rather than adverbial, and that the construction is harsh.

greek: Ἀλλ᾽ οὐ τοιοῦτον, ὁποῖον καὶ ἐφ᾽ ἡμῶν γινόμενον ὁρῶμεν; Λόγον γὰρ τινα προβάλλοντες, λόγον γεννῶμεν, οὐ ἀποτομὴν, ὡς ἐλαττωθῆναι τὸν ἐν ἡμῖν λόγον προβαλλόμενοι.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.134 (printed p.124), read on page image. Variant in Otto's note (PDF 77 of the 1969 Otto file): 'οὐ κατ᾽ ἀποτομήν' (with κατ᾽).
english: ...just as we see happening among ourselves: for when we give out some word, we beget the word; yet not by abscission, so as to lessen the word [which remains] in us, when we give it out:
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.124. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: Justin compares the Father's begetting of the Logos to uttering a word, which begets the word without cutting it off from the speaker.
use: answer to objection (against 'division' or diminution of the Father's substance)
limits: Analogy only, not a definition; Trollope n.10 notes Irenaeus (Her. II.13) rejected such analogies as Gnostic-tinged. The Greek 'οὐ ἀποτομὴν' (Trollope) differs from Otto's 'οὐ κατ᾽ ἀποτομήν'. Trollope's text punctuates with a question mark after 'ὁρῶμεν' (Otto's correction).

greek: Καὶ ὁποῖον ἐπὶ πυρὸς ὁρῶμεν ἄλλο γινόμενον, οὐκ ἐλαττουμένου ἐκείνου ἐξ οὗ ἡ ἄναψις γέγονεν, ἀλλὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μένοντος, καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἀναφθὲν καὶ αὐτὸ ὃν φαίνεται, οὐκ ἐλαττῶσαν ἐκεῖνο οὗ ἀνήφθη.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.134 (printed p.124), read on page image. Otto's note (PDF 77 of the 1969 Otto file) prints 'γενόμενον' for 'γινόμενον'.
english: and just as we see also happening in the case of a fire, which is not lessened when it has kindled [another], but remains the same; and that which has been kindled by it likewise appears to exist by itself, not diminishing that from which it was kindled.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.124. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: As one fire kindled from another loses nothing, so the begotten Logos does not diminish the Father from whom it came.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (no diminution of the Father); also an answer to objection on 'division'
limits: The fire image shows non-diminution, not identity of substance (no homoousios). Justin uses the image in one direction only; the kindled fire is said to 'appear to exist by itself', which Unitarians can read as a separate being.

greek: ποτὲ δὲ ἀρχιστράτηγον ἑαυτὸν λέγει, ἐν ἀνθρώπου μορφῇ φανέντα τῷ Ναυῆ Ἰησοῦ· ἔχει γὰρ πάντα προσονομάζεσθαι, ἐκ τε τοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν τῷ πατρικῷ βουλήματι, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς θελήσει γεγενῆσθαι.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.134 (printed p.124), read on page image (the first clause ends the list in J6-01). Trollope n.7 notes that the vulgate 'ἔχειν' is erroneous and was corrected by Otto to 'ἔχει'.
english: and on another occasion He calls Himself Captain, when He appeared in human form to Joshua the son of Nave (Nun). For He can be called by all those names, since He ministers to the Father's will, and since He was begotten of the Father by an act of will;
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.124. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: The Logos is called by all the names listed because he serves the Father's will and was begotten from the Father by will.
use: explanation of hard pass (begotten by 'will' answers the temporal-generation worry: the begetting is by the Father's will, not by necessity)
limits: The 'by will' answer does not say whether the begetting is eternal; Justin uses 'ἀρχή' and 'πρὸ πάντων' in the same chapter (see J6-01, J6-12). Opponents (Arians) read 'will' as the Father's decision to create a first being.

ref: 61.1 (Trollope 'LXI'; the Wisdom identification, continued onto p.125)
greek: Μαρτυρήσει δέ μοι ὁ λόγος τῆς σοφίας, αὐτὸς ὁ οὗτος ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν ὅλων γεννηθεὶς, καὶ λόγος καὶ δύναμις καὶ δόξα τοῦ γεννήσαντος ὑπάρχων.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF pp.134-135 (printed pp.124-125), read on page image (the sentence runs over to 'καὶ δύναμις' on p.125).
english: The Word of Wisdom, who is Himself this God begotten of the Father of all, and Word, and Wisdom, and Power, and the Glory of the Begetter, will bear evidence to me, when He speaks by Solomon the following:
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope pp.124-125. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: The Word of Wisdom is the same God begotten of the Father of all, and is also Word, Power and Glory of the begetter.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (the Wisdom of Prov 8 is identified as God, begotten and yet 'Word, Power and Glory' of the Father)
limits: 'Power' (δύναμις) is the word behind the brief's question whether the Spirit is only a 'power' of God. Justin does not separate Logos and Spirit here. Do not read 'begotten' as temporal without J6-06.

ref: 61.2 (LXX Prov 8:22-25 as quoted; the quotation runs to Prov 8:36 in Justin)
greek: Κύριος ἔκτισέ με ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς ἔργα αὐτοῦ. Πρὸ τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐθεμελίωσέ […] ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸ τοῦ τὴν γῆν ποιῆσαι, καὶ πρὸ τοῦ τὰς ἀβύσσους δεῆσαι, πρὸ τοῦ τὰς πηγὰς προελθεῖν τῶν ὑδάτων, πρὸ τοῦ τὰ […] πρὸ δὲ πάντων τῶν βουνῶν γεννᾷ με.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.135 (printed p.125), read on page image; the damaged words are marked [...]. Trollope n.20: the MSS have 'ὁδὸν'; 'ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν' is the LXX reading restored by Otto.
english: If I shall declare to you what happens daily, I shall call to mind events from everlasting, and review them. The Lord made me the beginning of His ways for His works. From everlasting He established me in the beginning, before He had made the earth, and before He had made the deeps, before the springs of the waters had issued forth, before the mountains had been established. Before all the hills He begets me.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.125. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: Justin applies Prov 8 to the Logos/Wisdom: the Lord made or begot it before creation and before the hills.
use: objection (the verb 'begets' and 'made me' are the temporal-generation worry) and supports Trinitarian reading (pre-existent Wisdom with the Father, Trollope n.20 and n.2 on p.125)
limits: The Greek 'ἔκτισέ' (made) and 'γεννᾷ' (begets) are both used of the same person; Arians cite 'ἔκτισέ'. The damaged words (marked […]) are not quoted; 'δεῆσαι' is as read on the image and in OCR, and its LXX form is not checked; the phrase 'ἐθεμελίωσέ με' is read here without 'με' (OCR and image both show 'ἐθεμελίωσέ' at the line end). The rest of the quotation (Prov 8:26-36) was read in OCR only.

ref: 60 (end) and 61 opening: Trypho's summary of the bush passage, then Justin's reply
greek: τὸν Θεὸν, τὸν ἀπὸ τῆς βάτου ὁμιλήσαντα τῷ Μωσεῖ, οὐ τὸν … τῶν ὅλων Θεὸν νοήσομεν γεγονέναι, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνον τὸν καὶ τῷ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τῷ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τῷ Ἰακὼβ ἀποδειχθέντα πεφανερῶσθαι, ὃς καὶ ἄγγελος τοῦ τῶν ὅλων ποιητοῦ Θεοῦ καλεῖται [...] Ἤδη μέντοι, ὦ […], ἀποδείξω ὅτι πρὸς τῇ Μωσέως ὀπτασίᾳ αὐτὸς οὗτος … καὶ ἄγγελος καλούμενος καὶ Θεὸς ὑπάρχων, ὥφθη … τῷ Μωσεῖ.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.133 (printed p.123), read on page image; words marked … are not legible. The first sentence is Trypho's summary; the second is Justin's reply.
english: Trypho: [...] we shall perceive that the God who communed with Moses from the bush was not the Maker of all things, but He who has been shown to have manifested Himself to Abraham and to Isaac and to Jacob; who also is called and is perceived to be the Angel of God the Maker of all things, because He publishes to men the commands of the Father and Maker of all things. Justin: Now assuredly, Trypho, I shall show that, in the vision of Moses, this same One alone who is called an Angel, and who is God, appeared to and communed with Moses.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.123 (ch.60 end). English: page unknown.
what_it_says: The Angel who appeared to Moses is the one who is also God, not the Maker of all things, and he is the Angel of the Maker, who announces the Father's commands.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (the Angel of the Lord is the divine Logos, distinct from the Father, Dial. 60 ends with the distinction) and objection (the 'angel' title, which Arians and Unitarians read as a created messenger)
limits: This is outside the assigned chapters (60 is not in J6). The Greek is mostly illegible on the image; only the words not marked with ellipses are read. The Trypho sentence is a paraphrase that Justin then answers, so it is not Justin's own assertion.

greek: Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ᾽ εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ᾽ ὁμοίωσιν, καὶ ἀρχέτωσαν τῶν ἰχθύων τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ τῶν πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ τῶν κτηνῶν, καὶ πάσης τῆς γῆς, καὶ πάντων τῶν ἑρπετῶν τῶν ἑρπόντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς ἄνθρωπον, κατ᾽ εἰκόνα Θεοῦ ἐποίησεν αὐτόν, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.136 (printed p.126), read on page image.
english: Let Us make man after our image and likeness. And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heaven, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over all the creeping things that creep on the earth. And God created man: after the image of God did He create him; male and female created He them.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.126. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: Gen 1:26 has God speaking in the plural ('Let Us make'), addressed to a second, distinct person.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (plural address), but Justin needs the next item to make it count
limits: The verse alone does not identify the second party; Justin argues it from Gen 3:22 (J6-10). Trollope n.11 records rabbinic readings (counsel with the works of heaven and earth, or with angels) and Kimchi's report that his father took the words as addressed to the elements.

ref: 62.1 (Trollope 'LXII'; Justin's list of rival readings of 'Let Us make')
greek: Καὶ ὅπως μὴ ἀλλάσσοντες τοὺς προλελεγμένους λόγους ἐκεῖνα λέγητε ἃ οἱ διδάσκαλοι ὑμῶν λέγουσιν, ἢ ὅτι πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ἔλεγεν ὁ Θεὸς, Ποιήσωμεν, ὁποῖον καὶ ἡμεῖς μέλλοντές τι ποιεῖν πολλάκις πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγομεν, Ποιήσωμεν· ἢ ὅτι πρὸς τὰ στοιχεῖα, τουτέστι τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ὁμοίως, ἐξ ὧν νοοῦμεν τὸν ἄνθρωπον γεγονέναι, Θεὸν εἰρηκέναι, Ποιήσωμεν.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.136 (printed p.126), read on page image.
english: And that you may not change the [force of the] words just quoted, and repeat what your teachers assert — either that God said to Himself, 'Let Us make,' just as we, when about to do something, oftentimes say to ourselves, 'Let us make;' or that God spoke to the elements, to wit, the earth and other similar substances of which we believe man was formed, 'Let Us make,'—
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.126. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: Justin lists two rival readings of 'Let Us make' (a soliloquy, or speech to the elements) and rejects them.
use: answer to objection (rival readings of 'Let Us make')
limits: Justin does not name the 'teachers' here. Trollope n.11 notes Thirlby's conjecture 'ἀλύσκοντες' for 'ἀλλάσσοντες' and says it is unsure. The rabbinic readings (counsel with works, angels) are in Trollope's note, not Justin's text.

ref: 62.2 (Trollope 'LXII'; Gen 3:22 introduced as the proof text for 'numerically distinct')
greek: …λόγους τοὺς εἰρημένους ὑπὸ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Μωϋσέως πάλιν ἱστορήσω, ἐξ ὧν […] ἀριθμῷ ὄντα ἕτερον καὶ λογικὸν ὑπάρχοντα, […] αὐτὸν ἐπιγνῶναι ἔχομεν. Εἰσὶ δὲ οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι· Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Θεός, Ἰδοὺ Ἀδὰμ γέγονεν ὡς εἷς ἐξ ἡμῶν, τοῦ γινώσκειν.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.136 (printed p.126), read on page image; the words between the brackets are not legible. Trollope n.18: the copula 'ὑπάρχοντα' is absent from the MSS and was restored by Otto after Thirlby.
english: I shall quote again the words narrated by Moses himself, from which we can indisputably learn that [God] conversed with some one who was numerically distinct from Himself, and also a rational Being. These are the words: 'And God said, Behold, Adam has become as one of us, to know good and evil.' Genesis 3:22
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.126. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: God spoke with someone numerically distinct from Himself and rational, as shown by 'as one of us' in Gen 3:22.
use: supports Trinitarian reading ('numerically distinct' is the key phrase; Justin's own word is 'ἀριθμῷ ὄντα ἕτερον')
limits: The participle 'ὑπάρχοντα' is an editorial restoration (Otto after Thirlby), not in the MSS per Trollope. 'ἕτερον' here is Justin's word for distinctness, and opponents may read it as 'different in kind' or 'another angel' (general objection, not sourced to a named author here). Gen 3:22 is a plural in Hebrew and LXX; the proof depends on Justin's reading.

greek: Οὐκοῦν εἶπων, ‘Ὡς εἷς ἐξ ἡμῶν, καὶ ἀριθμὸν τῶν συνόντων, καὶ τὸ ἐλάχιστον δύο μεμήνυκεν. Οὐ γὰρ, ἐπεὶ ἡ παρ᾽ ὑμῖν λεγομένη αἵρεσις δογματίζει, φαίην ἂν ἐγὼ ἀληθὲς εἶναι, ἢ οἱ ἐκείνης διδάσκαλοι ἀποδεῖξαι δύνανται, ὅτι πρὸς ἀγγέλους ἔλεγεν, ἢ ὅτι ἀγγέλων ποίημα ἦν […]
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.137 (printed p.127), read on page image; the end of the last clause is not legible.
english: In saying, therefore, 'as one of us,' [Moses] has declared that [there is a certain] number of persons associated with one another, and that they are at least two. For I would not say that the dogma of that heresy which is said to be among you is true, or that the teachers of it can prove that [God] spoke to angels, or that the human frame was the workmanship of angels.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.127. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: 'As one of us' shows a plurality of at least two persons, and Justin rejects the Jewish-sect view that God spoke to angels.
use: answer to objection (the angel reading of 'as one of us') and supports Trinitarian reading (at least two persons)
limits: 'Heresy said to be among you' is a Jewish sect (Trollope/Otto identify it only as the Jews' view; not named). Justin's 'number of persons' is the plural argument, not a Nicene 'one ousia'. Opponents answer that 'us' is the court of angels or the heavenly council.

ref: 62.4 (Trollope 'LXII'; the Offspring with the Father before all creatures, identified as Wisdom of Prov 8)
greek: Ἀλλὰ τοῦτο τὸ τῷ ὄντι ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς προβληθὲν γέννημα πρὸ πάντων τῶν ποιημάτων συνῆν τῷ πατρὶ, καὶ τούτῳ ὁ πατὴρ προσομιλεῖ, ὡς ὁ λόγος διὰ τοῦ Σολομῶνος ἐδήλωσεν, ὅτι ἀρχὴ πρὸ πάντων τῶν ποιημάτων τοῦτ᾽ αὐτὸ καὶ γέννημα ὑπὸ Θεοῦ ἐγεγέννητο, ὃ σοφία διὰ Σολομῶνος καλεῖται.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 1, PDF p.137 (printed p.127), read on page image.
english: But this Offspring, which was truly brought forth from the Father, was with the Father before all the creatures, and the Father communed with Him; even as the Scripture by Solomon has made clear, that He whom Solomon calls Wisdom, was begotten as a Beginning before all His creatures and as Offspring by God, who has also declared this same thing in the revelation made by Joshua the son of Nave (Nun).
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope p.127. English: page unknown.
what_it_says: The Offspring brought forth from the Father was with the Father before all creatures, and is the Wisdom of Prov 8 begotten as a Beginning.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (co-presence with the Father, 'the Father communed with Him') and objection (temporal-generation worry from 'before all' and 'Beginning')
limits: 'Before all creatures' is the temporal wording opponents exploit; Justin does not say the begetting is eternal. 'προβληθὲν' (put forth) and 'γέννημα' (offspring) are the generation words, not 'ὁμοούσιος'.

ref: 128.1 (Justin's own phrase 'ἐν τοῖς προειρημένοις … εἶπον'; the 'not by abscission' passage). Greek is quoted in Otto's note on Tatian; Justin's own printed page not located.
greek: ἐν τοῖς προειρημένοις διὰ βραχέων τὸν λόγον ἐξήτασα, εἶπον τὴν δύναμιν ταύτην γεγεννῆσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρός, δυνάμει καὶ βουλῇ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ κατ᾽ ἀποτομήν, οὃρ ἀπομεριζομένης τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς οὐσίας, ὁποῖα τὰ ἄλλα πάντα μεριζόμενα καὶ τεμνόμενα οὐ τὰ αὐτά ἔσειν ἃ καὶ πρὶν τμηϑῆ[ναι]
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi (3rd ed., Jena 1876-81), reprint Wiesbaden: Sändig 1969, file archive.org corpusapologeta03moragoog; note quoting Dial. 128 on PDF p.77 (printed p.24, from the running head read in the text layer). OCR: 'οὃρ' (probably ὡς or οὐδ᾽) and 'ἔσειν' are unclear; the end 'τμηϑῆ-' is cut off. Trollope vol. 2 (PDF pp.128-129) was checked for the same sentence and is too garbled to quote.
english: and when I asserted that this power was begotten from the Father, by His power and will, but not by abscission, as if the essence of the Father were divided; as all other things partitioned and divided are not the same after as before they were divided:
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Otto printed p.24 (Greek, quoted); English page unknown; Trollope vol. 2 Greek not located legibly.
edition: Otto 1969 reprint (Greek, in Otto's note); ANF vol. 1, 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin says the power was begotten from the Father by His power and will, not by cutting off, as if the Father's essence were divided, since divided things are no longer what they were before.
use: answer to objection (against 'division' of the Father's essence, the core of the 'abscission' objection)
limits: This is Justin's own argument, but the Greek is known only from Otto's quotation (OCR); Justin's denial concerns 'this power' (the Logos) and does not extend to any further claim about the Father's essence. Justin uses the analogy of the 'division' of things which are then 'not the same' - which cuts against the Nicene 'one substance'. Otto's note to Tatian discusses 'ἀποκοπή' vs 'μερισμός' at length.

ref: 128.2-128.3 (the opponents' 'sun's light' image, which Justin reports and rejects)
greek: …ται, λέγουσι, δύναμιν αὐτοῦ προπηδᾷν ποιεῖ, καὶ ὅταν βούληται, πάλιν ἀναστέλλει εἰς ἑαυτόν. Κατὰ τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους ποιεῖν αὐτὸν διδάσκουσιν.
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 2 (ed. W. Trollope, Cambridge/London 1846), PDF p.130 (printed p.120), read from the PDF text layer and djvu OCR only; the image is too poor to check. The Greek of the sun-image sentence itself (ἥλιος / φῶς) is not legible in the OCR and is not quoted.
english: ...but maintain that this power is indivisible and inseparable from the Father, just as they say that the light of the sun on earth is indivisible and inseparable from the sun in the heavens; as when it sinks, the light sinks along with it; so the Father, when He chooses, say they, causes His power to spring forth, and when He chooses, He makes it return to Himself. In this way, they teach, He made the angels.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope vol. 2 p.120 (OCR). English: page unknown.
what_it_says: Justin reports that opponents liken the Son to sunlight which goes out and returns, a power the Father sends out and recalls at will.
use: objection (the emanation/sunlight model that Justin rejects in the next lines)
limits: The SUN-RAY analogy is NOT Justin's own image: it is the opponents' view, which Justin rejects (see J6-13 and J6-16). The brief's attribution to Justin is wrong. Greek only partly legible.

ref: 128.1 (opening of ch.128: Christ 'Lord and God, the Son of God')
greek: καὶ ὅτι κύριος ὢν ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ Θεὸς Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων, […] ἐν πυρὶ δόξῃ, ὡς ἐν τῇ βάτῳ, πέφανται, καὶ ἐπὶ […] τῆς γεγενημένης ἐπὶ Σόδομα, ἀποδέδεικται
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 2, PDF p.129 (printed p.119), read from the text layer and djvu OCR; words marked […] are illegible. Not checked on the image.
english: And that Christ being Lord, and God the Son of God, and appearing formerly in power as Man, and Angel, and in the glory of fire as at the bush, so also was manifested at the judgment executed on Sodom, has been demonstrated fully by what has been said.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope vol. 2 p.119 (OCR). English: page unknown.
what_it_says: Christ is Lord and God, the Son of God, who appeared to the patriarchs in power, as angel, and in fire at the bush and at Sodom.
use: supports Trinitarian reading ('God of God' phrase: Son of God and God)
limits: 'God of God' is 'Θεὸς Θεοῦ' in the OCR and is not a Nicene 'Light from Light' or 'homoousios'. The English says 'Son of God' and 'Lord and God'. The Greek is a summary sentence of what Justin has argued and is partly illegible.

ref: 129.1 (Gen 19:24 as proof of two in number)
greek: Ὅταν λέγῃ, Ἔβρεξε κύριος πῦρ παρὰ κυρίου ἐκ […] μὲν ἐπὶ γῆς ὄντα, ὃς φησι καταβεβηκέναι ἰδεῖν τὴν κραυγὴν […]δόμων, τὸν δὲ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 2, PDF p.130 (printed p.120), read from the text layer and djvu OCR; the damaged words are marked […].
english: When Scripture says, 'The Lord rained fire from the Lord out of heaven,' the prophetic word indicates that there were two in number: One upon the earth, who, it says, descended to behold the cry of Sodom; Another in heaven, who also is Lord of the Lord on earth, as He is Father and God; the cause of His power and of His being Lord and God.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope vol. 2 p.120 (OCR). English: page unknown.
what_it_says: Gen 19:24 shows two Lords, one on earth (who went down to Sodom) and one in heaven, who is Lord of the Lord on earth, Father and God.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (the Lord-from-the-Lord proof of two)
limits: Justin's 'Lord of the Lord' argument assumes 'Lord' and 'God' name the Son; opponents may read the 'Lord on earth' as an angel (cf. the 'Angel of the Lord' of Gen 18-19); this is a general objection, not sourced here. Greek only partly legible.

ref: 129.2 (Gen 3:22 'as one of us' is indicative of number)
greek: καὶ πάλιν ὅταν λέγῃ ὁ Θεὸς […] τὸν Θεὸν ἐν ἀρχῇ, Ἰδοὺ Ἀδὰμ γέγονεν ὡς εἷς ἐξ ἡμῶν, καὶ αὐτὸ ἀριθμοῦ δηλωτικόν ἐστιν, […] χωροῦσιν οἱ λόγοι, ὡς ἐξηγεῖσθαι ἐπιχειροῦσιν
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 2, PDF p.131 (printed p.121), read from the text layer and djvu OCR; the gaps are marked […]. 'χωροῦσιν' in OCR appears without 'οὐ', which the English requires ('do not admit').
english: Again, when the Scripture records that God said in the beginning, 'Behold, Adam has become like one of Us,' Genesis 3:22 this phrase, 'like one of Us,' is also indicative of number; and the words do not admit of a figurative meaning, as the sophists endeavour to affix on them, who are able neither to tell nor to understand the truth.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope vol. 2 p.121 (OCR). English: page unknown.
what_it_says: 'Like one of Us' indicates number, and the words cannot be read figuratively.
use: supports Trinitarian reading (plural 'number' argument, repeated from J6-10)
limits: Repetition of the Gen 3:22 argument; the 'sophists' are the rabbis/teachers. Not an argument for 'one substance'.

ref: 129.3 (Prov 8 as applied: the Offspring begotten by the Father before all creatures is 'numerically distinct' from its begetter)
greek: Νοεῖτε, ὦ ἀκροαταὶ, εἴ γε καὶ τὸν νοῦν […] Ἐν καὶ ὅτι γεγεννῆσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τοῦτο τὸ γέννημα […] ἁπλῶς τῶν κτισμάτων ὁ λόγος ἐδήλου
greek_edition: Trollope 1846, vol. 2, PDF p.131 (printed p.121), read from OCR only. 'ἁπλῶς' appears in the OCR where the English implies 'πρὸ πάντων'; 'ἀριθμῷ ἕτερον' is not visible in the OCR of this passage.
english: When I repeated these words, I added: You perceive, my hearers, if you bestow attention, that the Scripture has declared that this Offspring was begotten by the Father before all things created; and that which is begotten is numerically distinct from that which begets, any one will admit.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1; rev. New Advent)
page: Greek: Trollope vol. 2 p.121 (OCR). English: page unknown.
what_it_says: The Offspring begotten by the Father before all creatures is numerically distinct from the Father who begets it.
use: supports Trinitarian reading ('numerically distinct' from the begetter) and answer to objection (the 'begotten before creation' worry is answered by distinctness of person)
limits: The English 'numerically distinct' is the ANF rendering of 'ἀριθμῷ ἕτερον' (not visible in the OCR of this passage). Justin says 'begotten before all things', which is still temporal wording. Greek only partly legible.
